meepoboard-eu.com.title: Good board, slow delivery
meepoboard-eu.com.text:
The delivery estimate was way off. Instead of 2-7 business days it was 3 weeks. 

The board (Rover) is great so far and mostly delivers what was promised. Real world range for me has so far been about 20 km on the low setting, on about +10 C temperatures, with some moderate uphills and riding mostly on asfalt spiced with some gravel roads. Faster modes eat battery more aggressivily, so it's some times a hard choise between more fun or more range. As it is pretty comfortable to ride, it would greatly benefit from a bigger battery, giving more range for longer sessions. As for how it handels with different kind of road surfaces, I haven't so far found a normal road that could not be ridden with confidence. The big tires eat everything up to pretty big curbs without the board trying to throw you off. 

So, only complaints so far are:
1. the delivery promise. Please give real time estimates instead of false promises.
2. range and battery size. Personally I could pay a little bit more for a bigger battery, as an extra option for example.

My first eboard and I'm totally hooked, most fun thing I have owned in years. Probably will need an upgrade to a bigger and faster board pretty soon, the appetite grows pretty fast :D

exwayboard.com.title: Exway Atlass Pro
exwayboard.com.text:
Honestly really disappointed with my recent experience with the Exway Atlas Pro ecosystem.

Before buying the Atlas Pro, I specifically chose Exway because I wanted a premium and highly customizable board that I could gradually upgrade into a serious off-road monster setup.

Unfortunately my experience has been the opposite.

First, my charger failed/burned after only the second charging session.

Then I upgraded to 175mm off-road tires and ordered the official AP-5H16W66T pulleys because:

- Exway references 175mm + 66T setups on their website,
- dealers sell 175mm kits with 66T pulleys,
- and multiple community posts mention 66T for 175mm tires.

However, the pulley physically does not fit my hubs.

Initially support told me I basically needed to push/install it harder, but later another support representative admitted that my Atlas Pro hub revision only supports 56T pulleys and is incompatible with 66T.

Apparently there are multiple undocumented hardware revisions and compatibility differences depending on the hub generation.

Now I am stuck running 175mm tires on 56T pulleys, which causes:

- weaker acceleration,
- weaker braking,
- lower efficiency,
- more drivetrain stress,
- and worse battery consumption.

I understand mistakes happen, but this has been extremely frustrating for such an expensive “premium” ecosystem.

The most disappointing part is the inconsistent compatibility information between:

- the website,
- dealers,
- community guidance,
- and Exway support itself.

At this point I’m honestly considering selling the board and moving to another brand because I originally bought into Exway for the promised upgrade ecosystem and customization potential.

Just wanted to share my experience in case someone else runs into the same Atlas Pro / 175mm / 66T compatibility situation.

exwayboard.com.title: At the end of the day, Exway doesn’t just sell boards—it sells lessons.
exwayboard.com.text:
Buying from Exway is like paying luxury prices for a front-row seat to your own disappointment.

This isn’t a product—it’s an experience. Specifically, the experience of wondering how something that looks so polished can perform so inconsistently. It’s almost impressive. Not in a good way—more like a case study in how to miss expectations with confidence.

The build quality feels like it was designed for unboxing videos, not actual use. Everything seems fine… until you actually ride it. Then it becomes a game of “what’s going to go wrong today?”

And reliability? Let’s just say trust evaporates faster than the battery life. You don’t ride an Exway board—you negotiate with it. Every session feels like you’re asking, “Are we doing this today, or are you going to embarrass me again?”

Customer experience doesn’t exactly save it either. Getting clear, reassuring support can feel like trying to get a straight answer out of a magic 8-ball—except the 8-ball might actually be more consistent.

At the end of the day, Exway doesn’t just sell boards—it sells lessons. Expensive ones. Mostly about regret, lowered expectations, and why “looks good online” should never be your buying criteria.

Would I recommend it? Only if your goal is to turn money into frustration at maximum efficiency.

exwayboardusa.com.title: When Ownership Becomes Obligation
exwayboardusa.com.text:
There is a quiet shift that happens with Exway—not a sudden failure, but a gradual unraveling.

At first, it feels manageable. A small issue. A fixable problem. Something temporary.

But it doesn’t stay that way.

Instead of a clean resolution like a refund or replacement, the process becomes a loop: parts arrive, instructions follow, problems persist. What looks like support begins to feel like deflection. Responsibility slowly moves—from the company to the customer.

You are no longer just riding the board. You are maintaining it.

This is where the experience becomes liminal. You exist between ownership and repair. The board is yours, but it doesn’t fully work. Support is present, but resolution is not. You are helped, but not relieved.

And then comes the real issue.

The battery enclosure—one of the most critical components—lacks durability. When it fails, when it physically detaches, the problem shifts from inconvenience to safety risk. At that point, incremental fixes are no longer enough. A full resolution is expected.

Yet the pattern continues.

Across multiple experiences, similar concerns appear: battery issues, inconsistent quality, and difficulty obtaining proper support. This suggests not an isolated defect, but a recurring pattern.

And that pattern erodes trust.

Because at its core, the issue is simple:

A product failed early. A refund was requested. It was not honored.

Everything that followed exists because of that moment.

So what remains is not just a defective product, but a prolonged state of unresolved ownership—where the customer is left maintaining something that should have worked from the start.

If you are considering Exway, understand this:

You may not just be buying a board.

You may be stepping into a process—one where ownership quietly becomes obligation.

Now this is my experience and obviously not everyone's but still, the company and it's employees should be held accountable and to a higher standard. I would of been happy to send back the deck and pay a little more money for a NEW current G2 or Zealot deck etc. Instead I was just issued a $59.99 refund and told they are out of those decks for a few weeks...

I was really excited to get into e-boarding and make this into a new hobby. Instead the company has left me with a horrible feeling and questioning is this actually for me...

backfireboardsusa.com.title: Anyone considering purchasing from them who might be new to the world of electric skateboards and particularly those that might be considering purchasing from abroad (outside of the USA).
backfireboardsusa.com.text:
Who is this review for? Anyone considering purchasing from them who might be new to the world of electric skateboards and particularly those that might be considering purchasing from abroad (outside of the USA).

Why is this important? If you are buying a replacement component, you may get caught in an extremely frustrating and expensive Tech Support & Sales loop. You might think tech support and sales as a loop might not be in the best interest of the consumer and you would be right but it works really well for Backfire.

How does that work? They won’t disclose clear and complete upgrade paths for replacing components on your existing hardware and you have to contact Tech Support and then they have you. Welcome to the Tech Support & Sales loop.

Why is this bad? For each of the following steps in the loop you may have to incur the following: cost of part + international shipping (could be 78%+ of cost of part)  + import duty and taxes (which can be considerably inflated due to high shipping costs) for example for a new 9 pin hub motor this cost me $189.00 + $5.75 (insurance) + $95.46 (shipping) = $290.21 (total). As a nice surprise £41 import duty & taxes charge.

What is the Tech Support & Sales loop?

You buy a replacement part for your board and discover that the part is for a new version of your board so you contact support. 
They propose that you solve the issue by purchasing another new component. (you pay cost + shipping + duty)
The part arrives, you discover that there are no instructions and there is another incompatible set of parts, you contact support.
They propose that you solve the issue by purchasing another new component. (you might pay cost + shipping + duty)
You discover that there are no instructions for the two new components that are designed to work together and they are unsafe to ride as is, you contact support.
They propose that you solve the issue by purchasing another new component specifically designed to make the two new components that were designed for each other safe to use together. (you might pay cost + shipping + duty)

What did I do? I tried to dispute these shipping costs as all of these could have been minimized into a single shipment had my request for support had been responded to with a complete upgrade path outlining everything that needed to be purchased and how it can be assembled and used together. Failing to do this should have as a show of good faith resulted in comping the cost of the remainder of the upgrade which they failed to disclose when asked directly.

evolveskateboards.com.au.title: I own an Evolve Skateboards GTR Bamboo…
evolveskateboards.com.au.text:
I own an Evolve Skateboards GTR Bamboo All Terrain. I had not used it for around 1.5 years after my last ride, where I experienced a serious fault that resulted in injury.

During that ride, the board developed a critical issue where it would cut out when braking. When this occurred, I attempted to restart the board multiple times in order to safely return home.

The board would power on intermittently and sometimes respond, but when I applied throttle input there was no forward movement. Shortly after, without consistent response to input, the board suddenly engaged and accelerated unexpectedly, causing me to be thrown backwards and I fell, breaking my elbow.

Due to this incident, I have not used the board since due to safety concerns.

The issue involved loss of braking control, intermittent power loss, and unpredictable acceleration behaviour, which presents a serious safety risk.

evolveskateboards.com.au.title: Title: Poor warranty handling – Evolve GTR Carbon
evolveskateboards.com.au.text:
I’ve had a very frustrating experience with Evolve regarding a new Evolve GTR Carbon board.

The board was defective straight out of the box – the belt was misaligned and scraping against the motor pulley. Because of this, I have never used the board.

I initially contacted the retailer (Ride + Glide), who did not take responsibility and referred me elsewhere. Since then, the case has gone through Evolve UK, Evolve EU, and Evolve HQ in Australia.

Evolve EU received the rear assembly for repair and replaced parts (rear strut and motor hanger). However, the issue was not resolved – the problem remains essentially unchanged after the repair.

Since then I have experienced:
- No response from Evolve EU
- Evolve UK referring me back to the retailer
- Evolve HQ stating the issue “is not a concern” and encouraging me to ride the board

It is not reasonable to expect a customer to use a brand new premium product where the drivetrain is clearly not functioning correctly and the belt is scraping.

The case is still unresolved, and I am left with an unused board that does not work as it should.

Based on this experience, I cannot recommend Evolve.

evolveskateboardsuk.co.uk.title: Board Lost, Threats Made, Delays, and No Resolution After Months
evolveskateboardsuk.co.uk.text:
I feel it’s important to share my experience with Evolve UK so other customers know what they may be dealing with.

I originally sent my Evolve Hadean in for repair. Evolve kept my board for months with very few updates. On 8 July, I received an email saying that if I did not pay the repair invoice within 30 days, my board would either be returned unrepaired at my cost or disposed of. Under that pressure, I paid the £567.40 invoice.

After paying, I then found out the battery they invoiced me for wasn’t even in stock. I was left waiting for over a month for the part to arrive, with no proactive communication, I had to keep chasing myself.

When the repair was finally completed, Evolve arranged return delivery through their chosen courier. On 17 September it was marked as “delivered”, but nothing was delivered. I reported this the same day.

After weeks of back-and-forth, I was told the courier could not provide GPS evidence and the board had been lost in transit. Evolve then admitted that their claim to DHL was denied because they had not been submitted the claim within DHL’s 21-day window — a delay caused by their handling.

More than seven weeks have passed. I’ve been left without my board, without the £567.40 service I paid for, and without any fair offer to compensate me for the loss of a working Hadean with a brand-new battery.

What concerned me most is that, when I tried to resolve this, Evolve UK quoted the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 against me - a law designed to protect consumers from traders. Using that legislation in this context felt inappropriate and intimidating for a customer simply asking to be compensated for a board lost in their care.

I’ve now had to issue a formal Letter Before Action, as I’ve exhausted every attempt to resolve this reasonably.

I’ve been an Evolve fan for years, but this has been the worst customer service experience I’ve ever had. I sincerely hope the parent company addresses how the UK distributor handles repairs and customer issues, because this has been unacceptable from start to finish.

ownboard.net.title: An expensive Unreliable kids toy
ownboard.net.text:
Unbeknownst to me the mini kt arrived with several stripped screws in the poorly designed motors. The outer replaceable pu is mounted onto 3mm aluminium and while loose it just warped and bent out of shape.

Then i was only getting 7 miles range and found what i believe to be counterfeit samsung 30q cells. I measured the amp hours with a watt meter and got around 4.5ah into my supposedly 6ah pack. I have genuine cells in my torches and the print is all wrong.

My supposedly waterproof boards battery display steamed up and died in the first week.

The customer service just pretend they cant understand you and accused me of being too fat.

I found slightly longer screws and used the spare pu rubbers id bought and managed to get it all back together at my expense. Also replaced the battery display and properly waterproofed it vs the bit of foam i removed. I gave it to my much younger 10 stone brother and he uses it to pop round the village just about. One day the brakes cut out on a hill and he hit a gate and now needs a thousand pounds worth of dental work or more. It was at around 90 percent charge so was unexpected.

In summary its a fake fire hazard and death trap with no customer service. I bought a mini er from another brand and they also sent me faulty 100mm wheels but they eventually sent me one new one while i suffered with the 90mm ones. This does nearly 20 miles and the motor bolts are on the inner edge so far less stress and less likely to need tightening every single day.

either go with another brand or just throw 400 quid out the car window now, save your teeth and dignity.

ownboard.net.title: Terrible quality, even worse customer service.
ownboard.net.text: Everything was great upon receiving my board. It arrived promptly from the US warehouse, even in time for Christmas - as it was a last min purchase for my husband. After using the board for about 1 week, though, the rear hub wheel loosened. We tried to fix it on our own by replacing the wheel with one of the backups it came with, but it loosened again shortly after. I contacted ownboard via email, and after waiting for what felt like forever for a response they asked if we replaced the hub wheel - I responded that yes, we tried this, but I believe the board is defective and would like a full exchange. Then, after waiting several more days, they responded that, instead of replacing the board, they are sending just a replacement hub wheel! So, it arrived, and my husband and I tried to remove the whole rear hub motor cover to replace the wheel and re-do the wiring but, lo and behold, THE REAR SCREWS ARE STRIPPED! So we cannot even replace the wheel. I have tried getting in touch via WhatsApp, email, and wechat, and have explained that this cannot be fixed. But instead of finally agreeing to send a replacement board they ask that I FIND A “FRIEND” to fix it, or that I send it to some person in Texas who “can help.” I’m sorry, but after spending $500 I shouldn’t also have to cover shipping to TX and then not even know who this person is that I’m sending it to, or if I’ll even get it back in working condition. This company is a scam. They refuse to stand behind their product even when it is defective and clearly needs to be replaced. I cannot even get back in touch with the representative to continue fighting for a replacement board. If I could give 0 stars I would. Will be reporting Ownboard to the BBB, and placing negative reviews across all other outlets as well. DO NOT BUY- STAY AWAY and save yourself the money and the headache.

ownboard.net.title: Ownboard Carbon Defective from the box
ownboard.net.text:
I ordered a board from the factory with a discount coupon of $ 100, they told me that they have a warehouse in Europe and if I buy another set of wheels and do not use the discount coupon, they will send it to me in 3 days.
I paid an extra $ 230. They sent me a tracking number on December 17 and I received it on the 28th, of course they wrote the address wrong and I had to look for it and deal with DPD.After unpacking it, I found that one of the motors was not working, I immediately uploaded a video and sent it to them. I was told to open it and switch the ESC cables. I did it and sent them a video with the result, now the other motor worked and the initial one stopped, their answer was that they would send me spare parts from China, which would take 3 months and I would have to repair the board myself.I read on their page that if you order the board from their warehouse and not from the factory if there is a problem they will refund your money. I wrote to them that I have no desire to repair their product which already had 70 km on the remote from the box for which I paid  ( 1150$ ) and to wait for spare parts from china for 3 months and I want my money back.
They refused me.Their response was that they would help me find the problem and send me parts to fix it myself. I paid an extra $ 230 to have it for up to 3 days and got a defective product that they want me to fix myself. They don't want to take it back, even though it's written on their page, and they don't want to give me my money back .My question is who are these unscrupulous people and what is going on here.
